notes: Identity verified from supplied full seven-page primary journal report: An exercise in self-replication: Replicating Shah, Mullainathan, and Shafir (2012); Anuj K. Shah, Sendhil Mullainathan, Eldar Shafir; Journal of Economic Psychology 75 (2019) 102127; DOI 10.1016/j.joep.2018.12.001. Methods, results, discussion and references supplied; no PDF supplied. This is the primary replication report, not the original 2012 source. Unassigned sides/fields are placeholders. First shot of each level: F(1, 972) = 115.79, P < 0.001, partial eta-squared = 0.106; first shot of the game: F(1, 972) = 2.47, P = 0.116, partial eta-squared = 0.003; points per shot among no-borrowing participants: F(1, 458) = 81.88, P < 0.001, partial eta-squared = 0.152. These are distinct tests of scarcity and focus; identical neutral descriptions do not distinguish them. The first and third are labelled Replicates; the second Similar pattern, much weaker. No target assigned by row order, numeric matching, or requested metric. Candidate statistics are notes only; no effect-size conversion. Candidate experiment-wide final participant N = 974. 1010 recruited; 36 excluded for missing subject ID or incorrect blueberry allotment. The final 974 participants cover the experiment, not necessarily the no-borrowing or borrowing-only test.
